Structured Practices for Consistent Performance — at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., our Standard Operating Practices form the foundation of quality, compliance and sustainable growth.

At Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., clearly defined and consistently implemented practices form the basis of reliable and efficient operations. This Standard Operating Practices (SOP) document serves as a structured framework designed to ensure uniformity, accountability and operational control across all functions.

As a manufacturer of pharmaceutical and healthcare formulations, a strong emphasis is placed on maintaining high standards of quality, regulatory compliance and responsible manufacturing. From material handling to final product dispatch, this document supports systematic execution of activities while ensuring safety, efficiency and adherence to applicable standards.

Each section of this document is developed to establish clarity in processes, minimise operational variability and align practices with the expectations of customers, regulatory authorities and other stakeholders. It enables effective coordination across functions while reinforcing a culture of discipline, consistency and continuous improvement.

This document is designed as a dynamic system, evolving with operational requirements and industry expectations. Regular updates and improvements ensure that practices remain relevant, effectiveand aligned with environmental responsibility, workplace safety and ethical business conduct.

blocks.text: At Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., we maintain a systematic approach to managing energy consumption across all operational activities. Energy usage is controlled through defined practices, efficient equipment utilisation and continuous monitoring mechanisms. We focus on minimising energy loss, improving process efficiency and ensuring responsible consumption across production and support functions. These practices contribute to operational efficiency while supporting environmental responsibility and sustainability objectives.
To define standardised practices for effective energy management, ensuring optimal utilisation of energy resources, improved operational efficiency and reduced environmental impact.

These practices apply to all areas of operations where energy is utilised, including manufacturing processes, utility systems, storage areas and supporting functions, ensuring consistent control and responsible usage across the organisation.
The following procedures reflects the established practices implemented to enhance energy efficiency, optimize resource utilization and minimize environmental impact in our operations.

body.text: At Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., energy conservation is integrated into operational practices through the adoption of advanced technologies, standardised equipment specifications and controlled usage mechanisms.

Defined procurement specifications are established to ensure the selection and use of energy-efficient equipment across all applicable operations.
Electronically Commutated (EC) fans and blowers are utilised to enable precise speed control, reduced power consumption and improved system efficiency.
EC systems support lower heat generation, reduced operational losses and consistent performance under continuous operating conditions.
Standardisation of IE3 efficiency motors is maintained across relevant systems to ensure higher energy efficiency compared to conventional motors.
IE3 motors contribute to improved starting performance, better thermal management and enhanced operational reliability.
Selection of energy-efficient equipment is aligned with recognised efficiency standards to support compliance and sustainability objectives.
Periodic evaluation of equipment performance is carried out to ensure continued efficiency and identify opportunities for improvement.
LED Lighting Conversion

All conventional fluorescent, incandescent and halogen lighting systems have been replaced with energy-efficient LED fixtures across production areas, packaging sections, warehouses and administrative offices.
LEDs are selected for their high lumen-per-watt efficiency and extended service life, ensuring optimal illumination with reduced power consumption.
This upgrade has contributed to noticeable reductions in lighting-related energy usage, along with lower maintenance requirements.
Motion Sensors

Motion sensors are installed in low-traffic areas such as storage rooms, corridors, utility areas and restrooms, ensuring that lighting is activated only when required.
These sensor-based systems help prevent unnecessary energy consumption during low-traffic hours.
Boiler Waste Heat Recovery

Boiler at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. generate significant thermal energy from flue gases during operation.
This heat is recovered using economizer systems, which extract thermal energy from high-temperature flue gases.
The recovered thermal energy is utilised for preheating boiler inlet-water and maintaining required temperatures in the infeed water to the boiler.
Utilisation of recovered heat reduces dependence on external fuel-based heating systems, thereby lowering overall energy consumption and associated carbon emissions.
Pipeline Thermal Insulation System

All hot water and steam pipelines connected to Boiler heat recovery systems are fitted with high-quality insulation to minimize thermal losses.
Insulation helps maintain consistent process temperatures, shortens heating cycle times and improves overall thermal efficiency.
Reduction in External Energy Consumption

By reusing internally generated heat, the system reduces reliance on external heating systems such as electric boilers or fossil-fuel-based heaters.
This results in: Lower energy consumption; Reduced fuel usage; A measurable decrease in carbon dioxide emissions
The initiative directly supports Naxpar’s sustainability and decarbonization goals, aligning with both internal targets and external environmental compliance frameworks.

steps.heading: Clean Fuel Adoption and Emission Reduction

body.text: Transition to Cleaner Fuel Systems

Conventional diesel-fired boiler systems have been replaced with LPG-fired boilers for steam generation processes.
The boiler system has been upgraded from a 1.2 Ton Diesel-fired boiler to a higher-capacity 2.0 Ton LPG-fired boiler to improve operational efficiency and support production requirements.
LPG is utilised as a cleaner fuel alternative due to its lower emission profile and improved combustion efficiency compared to diesel.
Boiler operations follow optimized fuel usage and preventive maintenance practices to maintain energy efficiency and operational reliability.
Fuel consumption and boiler performance are periodically monitored to ensure efficient system operation.
Replacement of diesel-based systems with LPG-fired boilers has resulted in reduced fuel-related emissions and improved environmental performance.
These initiatives support Naxpar Pharma’s environmental management and sustainability commitments.
Emission Reduction and Environmental Impact

Reduction in diesel consumption has directly contributed to a decrease in carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions generated during operations.
Cleaner combustion of LPG supports lower emission of particulate matter and other air pollutants.
Implementation of cleaner fuel systems aligns with environmental compliance requirements and air quality standards.
Continuous efforts are maintained to minimise the carbon footprint associated with manufacturing activities.

Naxpar undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into:

Scope 1 – Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from boilers, generators and manufacturing equipment.
Scope 2 – Indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations.
Scope 3 – Other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities (e.g., raw material transportation, supplier emissions) and downstream activities (e.g., product distribution, waste disposal and employee commuting).

To support this process, Naxpar maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third-party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations.

By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, Naxpar Pharma strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

Technologies for water reuse, efficient cooling systems and rainwater harvesting are implemented to minimise consumption, while water audits, risk assessments and wastewater quality monitoring ensure responsible management and regulatory compliance. Control measures are established to prevent groundwater contamination and appropriate treatment processes are in place for removal of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) from wastewater, supporting sustainable water use and reduced environmental impact.
To ensure efficient use, conservation and responsible management of water resources while minimising environmental impact and maintaining regulatory compliance.

This applies to all operations and activities at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. where water is utilised, including production processes, utility systems, wastewater treatment and supporting functions, ensuring consistent control, monitoring and responsible water management across the organisation.

body.text: Influent Monitoring

Effluent generated from manufacturing and utility operations is collected and routed to the ETP for treatment.
Key parameters such as pH, temperature, TDS, COD and flow rates are monitored regularly to ensure proper treatment performance.
Effluent Treatment

Wastewater generated from manufacturing and utility operations is treated through a multi-stage treatment process within the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP). These stages include primary treatment for removal of suspended solids, secondary biological treatment for degradation of organic matter and tertiary treatment for further purification and polishing of the treated effluent.
During these treatment stages, residual Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), intermediates and other pharmaceutical compounds present in the wastewater are reduced through chemical neutralization processes. These processes help break down complex pharmaceutical residues and minimize their presence in the treated water.
Electrolyte or coagulant chemical such as ferric alum is added in controlled quantities in the neutralization tank, while air blowers ensure proper mixing and floc formation for effective removal of suspended contaminants.
Advanced treatment methods such as activated carbon adsorption or chemical oxidation are applied where required to further reduce trace pharmaceutical compounds. The treatment method is selected based on periodic assessment of effluent characteristics and API load.
Treated effluent is regularly monitored for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS and residual API levels to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory standards. Any deviation in treatment efficiency is reported to the EHS team and corrective actions are implemented promptly.
Water Recovery and Reuse

Treated water suitable for reuse is stored in designated storage tanks and reused for non-critical applications such as floor cleaning, utility washing, cooling systems and other auxiliary activities.
Sampling & Testing
Treated water is sampled periodically and analyzed for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS and suspended solids to verify compliance with internal standards and regulatory limits.

Any deviation in treatment performance or water quality is immediately reported to the EHS Manager or designated responsible personnel.
Corrective actions may include adjusting chemical dosing, modifying operational parameters, conducting equipment maintenance, or increasing monitoring frequency.
All deviations and corrective actions are recorded and reviewed to ensure effective resolution.

Operators ensure that tanks, pumps, pipelines and surrounding work areas are maintained in clean condition after operations.
Shutdown procedures for the ETP systems are carried out according to operational guidelines.
Daily records of operational parameters, water quality results and maintenance activities are maintained.

The EHS department is notified immediately and corrective measures are implemented.
Incident details are documented and preventive measures are reviewed to avoid recurrence.

Treated water recovered through the ETP is utilized for various non-potable applications within the facility to promote efficient water utilization and reduce dependence on freshwater sources. Typical reuse applications include:

Cooling Systems: Treated water recovered from the ETP systems is utilized in cooling towers or condenser circulation systems to support heat exchange processes within manufacturing and utility operations. This helps maintain efficient cooling performance while reducing reliance on fresh water sources.
Horticulture: Treated water recovered from ETP operations is used for gardening purposes in the plant premises to maintain green-belt area.
Cleaning and Construction Activities: External areas of the plant are cleaned using this treated water and construction/civil related requirements are also fulfilled using this treated water.

Recycled water is allocated based on operational requirements and quality suitability. Storage tanks, transfer pipelines and valves are inspected regularly to ensure safe handling and prevent contamination. All reuse volumes are recorded in the Water Reuse Log Sheet and any deviation in quality or supply is reported to the Utilities Supervisor for corrective action.
Water Usage Optimization

Water-Efficient Washing & Cleaning Practices: All washing and cleaning tasks are performed in accordance with standardized work instructions designed to ensure effective cleaning with minimal water use. These instructions specify:
Nozzle Type & Spray Pattern: Use of high-pressure, low-flow nozzles and controlled-spray systems for optimal coverage.
Cleaning Sequence: A structured top-to-bottom process, moving from cleaner to dirtier areas to avoid repeated washing.
Maximum Duration: Fixed time limits for each cleaning task to maintain consistency and prevent water wastage.

To support these practices, all equipment is maintained routinely to ensure accurate flow control, avoid leakages and sustain efficiency. Cleaning schedules are designed to balance hygiene needs with water conservation, preventing redundant or unnecessary washing activities. Additionally, all pharmaceutical-grade cleaning and sanitising agents used in the facility are low-rinse formulations, enabling effective cleaning without the need for extra rinse cycles or additional water beyond the specified limits. Treated water recovered from the on-site water treatment system is reused for non-potable cleaning activities such as external floor washing, The quality of reused water is verified regularly as per internal testing procedures.

Water-Efficient Cooling Systems: Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. operates a closed-loop water cooling system to support efficient water use in its manufacturing operations. The system recirculates cooling water within a closed circuit, reducing the need for freshwater intake and minimizing water losses.
To maintain water efficiency, the Company follows the following operating practices:
Continuous recirculation and reuse of cooling water.
Regular monitoring of system performance, including water levels, temperature and pressure.
Routine inspection of pumps, pipelines and valves to identify and address leaks.
Preventive maintenance of cooling equipment to ensure efficient operation.
These practices help optimize water consumption, reduce water wastage and support sustainable water management across operations.
Rainwater Harvesting

To reduce dependency on groundwater and promote sustainable water use practices in line with government regulations, Naxpar has implemented a robust rainwater harvesting system integrated into its facility infrastructure.

Strategic Rooftop Collection: Rainwater is collected from the rooftop surfaces of production blocks, utility areas and administrative buildings. The collected rainwater is directed through a network of drainage channels and downpipes towards designated Rainwater Harvesting (RWH) pits located within the facility premises.
Groundwater Recharge Infrastructure: The harvested rainwater is conveyed to dedicated RWH pits designed to facilitate the infiltration of water into the ground. This process supports the natural replenishment of the local groundwater table and enhances aquifer recharge. Periodic inspection and maintenance of the collection system and recharge structures are conducted to ensure effective rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge.

As part of its environmental risk management and regulatory compliance framework, Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. has established structured groundwater and soil protection measures within its pharmaceutical manufacturing and chemical handling operations.

Engineered Containment Systems: RCC flooring with chemical-resistant coating and designated collection pits have been constructed in tant coatings and designated collection pits are provided in solvent storage, reaction and handling areas. These engineered containment systems ensure that any accidental spills or leakages remain confined within a controlled boundary, preventing percolation into the soil and safeguarding underlying groundwater resources.
Safe Chemical Storage Practices: Process chemicals, including solvents and reagents are stored in sealed, corrosion-resistant drums and tanks that are clearly labelled and positioned within designated storage zones equipped with secondary containment arrangements. This controlled storage practice significantly minimizes the possibility of uncontrolled discharge and environmental contamination.
Employee Training & Awareness: Periodic training sessions are conducted to ensure employees understand safe chemical handling, transfer procedures, spill prevention methods and wastewater management practices. These awareness programs strengthen operational discipline and reduce the risk of groundwater contamination incidents.
Inspection & Preventive Maintenance: Hazardous material storage areas, pipelines and transfer systems are routinely inspected and maintained to preserve containment integrity. Operational protocols include monitoring of storage conditions, scheduled leak detection checks and immediate implementation of corrective measures in the event of any irregularities.
Documentation & Compliance Monitoring: Detailed documentation and systematic record-keeping are maintained for chemical inventories, inspection reports, maintenance logs and employee training activities. This structured compliance framework supports adherence to environmental regulations and promotes continuous improvement in contamination prevention and environmental protection performance.

Wastewater Quality Assessment:
Wastewater samples are collected from treatments inlet, each treatment stage and the final treated effluent. This enables a comprehensive evaluation of contaminant levels across the treatment process.
Samples are tested for key environmental indicators such as pH, Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Total Suspended Solids (TSS)and Ammoniacal Nitrogen. These tests are performed using standard analytical methods to ensure accuracy and consistency.
By testing the quality of treated effluent used internally reuse water is routinely monitored to ensure it meets internal specifications and safety parameters.
Detailed records are maintained for each sampling and testing activity. This includes sample logs, test reports, treatment system observations and any corrective actions taken in case of non-compliance. These records support internal audits, statutory reporting and continuous environmental performance improvement.

The Air Pollution Management Standard Operating Practices (SOP) at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. outline the practices implemented to prevent, monitor and manage air emissions arising from manufacturing and utility operations. As the Company manufactures liquid formulations, the potential for particulate matter generation is inherently limited. Air emission management therefore focuses on maintaining efficient operations, preventing unnecessary emissions and ensuring compliance with applicable environmental requirements.

The SOP includes measures such as controlled manufacturing practices, preventive maintenance of utility equipment, periodic ambient air quality and stack emission monitoring and regular review of environmental performance. These practices help ensure that emissions remain within prescribed regulatory limits and support the Company's commitment to responsible environmental management.

To establish standardized practices for the prevention, monitoring and management of air emissions arising from manufacturing and utility operations, ensuring compliance with applicable environmental regulations, minimizing environmental impact and promoting continual improvement in environmental performance.
These practices apply to all operations and utility systems at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. that generate air emissions, noise, or odour, ensuring consistent control and compliance across the facility.

body.text:
We at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. manufacture liquid formulations and does not undertake tablet manufacturing or other powder-intensive operations that typically generate significant particulate matter emissions. As a result, the risk of particulate matter generation is minimized at the source through the nature of the manufacturing process.

To further mitigate particulate matter emissions, manufacturing activities are conducted in controlled process areas and in accordance with established operating procedures. Raw materials are handled carefully to prevent unnecessary releases and routine housekeeping practices are implemented to maintain clean operational areas and prevent the accumulation of particulate matter.

Equipment and utility systems are regularly inspected and maintained to ensure efficient operation and to minimize the potential for unintended emissions. In addition, periodic ambient air quality monitoring is conducted through approved laboratories to assess air quality parameters and verify compliance with applicable environmental regulations and statutory requirements.

Through the use of liquid-based manufacturing processes, preventive maintenance practices, controlled operations and regular air quality monitoring, the Company effectively minimizes particulate matter emissions and maintains ambient air quality within prescribed regulatory limits.

Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. has undertaken a fuel transition initiative by replacing its High-Speed Diesel (HSD)-fired boiler with an LPG-fired boiler for utility operations. This transition was implemented to reduce air emissions associated with fuel combustion, as LPG is a cleaner-burning fuel with significantly lower sulphur content and improved combustion efficiency compared to HSD. As a result, the potential generation of sulphur oxides (SO₂), particulate matter and other combustion-related pollutants has been substantially reduced.

To further minimize emissions, the Company operates the boiler under controlled conditions and implements a preventive maintenance program covering burners, fuel supply systems and associated equipment. Regular inspection, tuning and maintenance activities are carried out to ensure efficient combustion, optimize fuel utilization and reduce the formation of nitrogen oxides (NOx).

Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) emissions are controlled through responsible chemical and solvent management practices. Raw materials and solvents are stored in designated containers and handled in accordance with established operating procedures to minimize evaporation losses, leaks and unintended releases. Material handling activities are conducted in controlled process areas and good housekeeping practices are maintained throughout the facility to prevent fugitive VOC emissions.

To verify the effectiveness of these controls, Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. conducts periodic stack emission monitoring and ambient air quality monitoring through approved external laboratories. Monitoring results are reviewed against applicable regulatory requirements to confirm compliance and evaluate environmental performance. Any observations identified through monitoring activities are assessed and addressed through corrective and preventive actions, where necessary.

Through the adoption of cleaner fuel technology, controlled operational practices, preventive maintenance, responsible chemical management and periodic environmental monitoring, Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. continuously works to minimize VOC, SO₂ and NOx emissions and reduce the environmental impact of its operations

Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. implements operational controls to minimize the generation and release of odours arising from chemical storage, handling and manufacturing activities. Chemical storage areas and production sections are maintained under controlled conditions and provided with adequate ventilation to prevent the accumulation and spread of odorous vapours.
Chemicals and raw materials are stored in designated containers and handled in accordance with established operating procedures to minimize spills, leaks and unnecessary vapour releases. Good housekeeping practices are maintained throughout the facility to ensure clean and orderly operations.
Routine inspections are conducted to identify any potential sources of odour within operational areas. Any odour-related observations or concerns reported by employees or external stakeholders are documented, investigated and addressed through appropriate corrective actions.
Personnel involved in chemical handling and manufacturing activities are trained on proper storage, transfer, spill prevention and odour control practices. Periodic refresher training is provided to reinforce awareness and support the effective implementation of odour management measures across the facility.

Foam-lined acoustic panels are installed around high-noise equipment such as air compressors, Diesel Generators and air handling units to absorb and reduce noise levels within Naxpar Pharma's Pvt. Ltd.'s manufacturing facilities.
All machinery is inspected and maintained routinely to ensure smooth operation and to minimize noise from mechanical wear, loose fittings, or vibrations. Faulty parts are replaced promptly.
Noise mapping and monitoring is carried out on a bi-annual basis across all production areas during both day and night shifts using calibrated sound level meters. Areas exceeding permissible limits are prioritized for additional controls.
Work rotation schedules are implemented to reduce prolonged exposure to high-noise zones. Ear protection (earplugs) is provided to employees in designated areas.
Workers are trained on hearing conservation practices and correct use of PPE. Monitoring results, maintenance logs and corrective actions are documented and reviewed periodically.
Earplugs are provided in high-noise areas and their usage is mandatory.

Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. has established an integrated waste management system as part of its commitment to environmental protection, occupational safety and regulatory compliance. The company follows a structured approach to manage waste generated from its pharmaceutical manufacturing and support activities, including raw material handling, processing, packaging, quality control, utilities and maintenance operations.

Waste management practices are systematically implemented across the facility with a focus on identification, segregation, minimisation, safe handling and environmentally responsible disposal. The key elements of the system include:

Identification of Waste Streams – All waste generated from various operations is identified, classified and recorded for proper management.
Segregation at Source – Waste is segregated at the point of generation into hazardous, non-hazardous and recyclable categories to ensure safe handling and disposal.
Waste Minimisation Practices – Process improvements and efficient use of materials are adopted to reduce the overall quantity of waste generated.
Safe Storage and Handling – Waste is stored in designated areas with proper labelling, containment and handling procedures to avoid spillage or contamination.
Authorised Disposal and Recycling – Waste is disposed of or recycled through authorised vendors and approved facilities in accordance with environmental regulations.

This SOP defines a systematic framework for managing waste at Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. It ensures that all waste streams are handled in a safe, organised and environmentally responsible manner. The objective is to maintain compliance with applicable environmental regulations, protect employee health and support sustainable operational practices.

This procedure is applicable to all operational and support areas of Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., covering the complete lifecycle of waste from its generation to final disposal or recycling. It includes waste generated from production processes, utilities, maintenance activities, laboratory and administrative functions, including both hazardous and non-hazardous categories.

body.text:
Segregation at Source: All waste must be placed immediately into the dedicated bins at the point of generation. No waste shall be mixed at any stage of handling, storage or transport.
Collection and Internal Transfer: Departmental staff or housekeeping personnel shall collect waste at scheduled intervals to avoid overflow, ensure cleanliness and prevent cross-contamination.
Temporary Storage: Each waste category shall be transferred to its designated interim storage area. Hazardous waste must remain in sealed and clearly labelled containers as per regulatory requirements until collected by authorized vendors.
Documentation & Register Updating: All waste quantities, categories and disposal details shall be recorded in the centralized Waste Stream Register. Department heads must verify weekly entries for accuracy.
Final Disposal: Waste shall be disposed of through authorized recyclers, hazardous-waste vendors as per the disposal method listed in the Waste Stream Mapping Table.
Monitoring: Supervisors and the EHS team shall routinely inspect segregation practices and provide refresher training to departments where non-compliance is observed.

Immediate Response: Any instance of mis-segregation or cross-contamination must be corrected immediately. Waste shall be re-segregated and handled according to the defined procedure.
Employee Retraining: Targeted training sessions are held for departments or shifts where errors are identified.
Root Cause Analysis: The EHS team shall investigate repeated non-compliance to identify process gaps and implement preventive measures.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All staff involved in waste handling, especially hazardous and chemical waste, are equipped with appropriate PPE including gloves, safety goggles, masks, aprons and closed footwear.
Spill Management: Trained personnel follow a documented Spill Response Protocol, using spill kits, absorbents and neutralizing agents. All incidents are recorded in the incident log.

Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. adopts a proactive, multi-tiered approach to minimize waste generation throughout its manufacturing and processing operations. Aligned with India’s environmental regulations and sustainability principles, the company emphasizes source reduction and process optimization over disposal, aiming to reduce its environmental footprint and enhance circularity.

steps.heading: Promotion of Material Reuse and Recovery

Identification of Recoverable Materials

A periodic waste stream audit is conducted to identify recyclable and recoverable materials generated during the product manufacturing process. These materials include, but are not limited to:

Recyclable Paper Waste: Clean cardboard, paper sheets and cartons from packaging areas and offices.
Recyclable Plastic Waste: Plastic films, wrappers and polybags from raw material receiving and packaging areas.

Collection and Segregation

Recyclable paper and plastic waste is segregated at production, utility and packing areas, collected and disposed to the scrap collection area.
Training sessions and awareness programs are conducted to ensure all staff understand the value of reuse and their role in achieving waste reduction goals.

Placement: Affixed to the upper front portion of each container for easy visibility during inspection and handling.

Transportation Execution and Post-Delivery Verification: Route Planning and Pre-Dispatch Checks: Transported via pre-approved, low-risk routes identified to minimize environmental and human health risks; Vehicles undergo pre-departure inspections for: Container integrity, Proper label display, Documentation readiness, Secure cargo placement
Delivery and Reconciliation at TSDF: On reaching the authorized Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facility (TSDF): Waste is unloaded under supervision; Quantity and type are verified against manifest entries; Any discrepancies are documented, reported and investigated; Form 10 is updated, signed and one copy is returned to Naxpar for records

At Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd., safe and efficient work procedures are established and implemented for all manufacturing and operational activities, covering processing, quality inspection, packaging, storage and dispatch operations.

These procedures are applicable and enforced for all employees, contractual staff, temporary workers, drivers and visitors across all operational areas, including production, processing, warehousing and logistics zones.

body.text:
Area-specific PPE (safety shoes, gloves, high-visibility vests where required) is mandatorily worn.
Machine guards are maintained intact and tampering is strictly prohibited.
Work areas are kept clean and obstruction-free, especially in packing and storage zones.
Unsafe conditions, near-misses and spills are reported immediately and addressed.
Floor markings, signage and designated zones (storage, walkways, loading bays) are clearly defined and followed.
Smoking, running in the warehouse and misuse of equipment are strictly prohibited.

Head Protection: Helmets are provided and used in loading/unloading or high-rack areas (if applicable).
Hand Protection: Appropriate gloves are issued and used during material handling and packing.
Foot Protection: Safety shoes are mandatory and enforced.
Eye Protection: Safety glasses are used where dust or flying particles are present (inspection, unpacking).
Body Protection: High-visibility jackets are worn in loading zones and during vehicle movement.

Only trained and authorised personnel may operate material-handling equipment such as, hand pallet trolleys, forklifts, high reach trucks or drum lifters used for raw materials and finished materials.
Conduct pre-use safety checks for equipment such as brakes, wheels, handles, safety locks and alarms (where applicable).
Do not exceed load capacities when stacking raw materials, r finished goods on pallets, racks, or trolleys.
Use proper lifting techniques—bend knees, keep back straight and hold loads close to the body—to prevent strain when handling heavy materials, drums, or cartons.
Utilise mechanical aids for heavy consignments or bulk loads to avoid manual overexertion and ensure operator safety.

Store raw materials packing materials and finished products in clearly labelled shelving systems or designated bin locations.
Keep different product types segregated (e.g., powders, liquids, packaged goods, accessories) to prevent mix-ups or cross-contamination.
Handle heavy drums, bulk containers and large consignments with care, ensuring a secure grip to avoid hand injuries.
Ensure racks, shelves and storage areas are not overfilled to prevent collapse or spillage of stored items.
Maintain dry, well-ventilated storage conditions to protect materials from moisture, contamination, or degradation.

Keep packing tables clean, organised and free from loose materials, debris, or packaging scraps.
Use ergonomic workstations and anti-fatigue mats for prolonged handling of products, including bottles, drums, cartons and accessory sets.
Dispose of packaging waste—such as cardboard, plastic liners and other scrap materials—only in designated collection bins.
Avoid excessive force when sealing containers, tying bundles, or strapping packages to prevent strain or musculoskeletal injuries.
Ensure accurate labelling and barcoding of each product type before dispatch, including batch numbers, product codes and handling instructions.

Do not use damaged electrical cords, plugs, extension boards, or portable equipment used in packing/dispatch areas.
Switch off all operational equipment—including tanks, pumps, filling machines and weighing/dispensing units—when not in use.
Report any sparking, burning smell, overheating, or abnormal noise immediately to the EHS Dept.
Keep all electrical panels unobstructed and ensure dry surroundings, especially in storage zones where flammable chemicals or materials are present.

Ensure delivery trucks, vans and cargo vehicles are completely stationary and secured before loading materials, drums, or packaged products.
Never stand beneath suspended loads during handling of bulk containers, pallets, or heavy consignments.
Use wheel stoppers, chocks and dock levellers where required.
Maintain a safe distance from moving vehicles, forklifts, or trolleys in dispatch areas.
Ensure cartons, drums, or pallets of materials and finished products are stacked evenly and secured properly to avoid tipping or shifting during transport.

Ensure safe handling, dispensing and storage of chemicals used in production, processing, cleaning, or adhesive/finishing operations.
Maintain up-to-date Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for all chemicals at easily accessible locations.
Provide chemical-specific PPE such as chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, aprons and face masks whenever handling solvents, reagents, cleaning agents, or other process chemicals.
Ensure proper ventilation or local exhaust systems in areas where vapours, fumes, or solvent-based chemicals are used.
Label all chemical containers clearly; never store chemicals in unmarked bottles or food containers.
Store chemicals in designated, well-ventilated storage areas away from heat, ignition sources and pharma materials.
Follow the trainings provided on safe chemical handling, spill response and emergency procedures.
Use spill kits immediately in case of chemical leaks; isolate the area and report to the supervisor.
Strictly prohibit eating, drinking, or smoking in areas where chemicals are stored or used.

Keep floors dry at all times; immediately clean water, oil, chemical, or solvent spills to prevent slips, especially in areas with powders, or liquid residues.
Use anti-slip mats in high-traffic zones such as packing, dispatch and storage walkways.
Ensure adequate lighting in storage rooms, inspection areas, stairways, loading bays and corridors.
Use handrails when ascending/descending stairs or ramps.
Secure loose cables, ropes, straps and packaging materials away from pathways.
Do not climb on pallets, drums, storage racks, or unstable stacks.
Use certified ladders or platforms for stacking/unstacking high rack items; ensure stability before use.
Wear slip-resistant safety shoes in all operational zones.

Immediately clean spills of chemicals, powders, residues and packaging waste to prevent slip, contamination and fire hazards in all operational areas.
Keep emergency exits, fire extinguishers and aisles clear at all times.
Maintain cleanliness in resting and eating areas; wash hands before breaks to avoid exposure to chemical residues, dust, or particulates.
Dispose of chemical, packaging and process waste only in designated collection bins or containers, following Naxpar’s hazardous and non-hazardous waste management protocols to ensure environmental compliance and safety.

Inform supervisors immediately if feeling unwell, exhausted, or experiencing difficulty due to dust exposure.
Take scheduled rest breaks to reduce fatigue during repetitive packing or material-handling tasks.
Stay hydrated, especially during high-activity periods or hot weather.
Use appropriate PPE such as dust masks, respirators, or chemical-rated masks when handling powders, fine particulates, or chemical materials to prevent inhalation hazards.

steps.heading: Ergonomic & RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) Prevention – Workstation Setup & Posture

body.text:
Ensure workstations lab benches, inspection tables, weighing stations and packing areas are adjusted to appropriate working height.
Maintain neutral posture: straight spine, relaxed shoulders, wrists aligned with forearms.
Use chairs with lumbar support and footrests where seated tasks are required for longer periods.

Rotate employees between tasks such as weighing, mixing, inspection, labelling and packaging to reduce continuous strain.
Take micro-breaks every 30–60 minutes to stretch shoulders, wrists, fingers and back.
Encourage short walking breaks for employees performing prolonged standing or sitting tasks.

Use ergonomic hand tools, pipettes, scoops, dispensers and cutters with cushioned grips to minimise strain.
Keep tools within easy reach to avoid overextension.
Use magnifying tools and proper lighting for detailed inspections, labelling, or sampling.

Avoid excessive force when handling heavy chemical containers, bulk powders, or packaged intermediates.
Keep wrists straight and avoid prolonged twisting while performing repetitive packing movements.
Follow the 20-20-20 eye rule for employees working with detailed inspection, documentation, or lab instruments.

Report all incidents, including minor injuries, slips, chemical spills, exposure to reagents, equipment malfunctions, or near-misses, to the Safety Officer immediately for prompt investigation.
All incidents will be recorded, reviewed and discussed in monthly safety committee meetings.

body.text: KPIs are defined based on departmental and organizational goals.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that all business activities of Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. are conducted ethically, transparently and in compliance with applicable laws and Company requirements. This procedure establishes controls to prevent bribery, corruption, kickbacks, improper gifts, conflicts of interest and other sensitive transactions that may improperly influence business decisions or result in personal gain.
This procedure applies to all employees, management personnel, contractors, consultants and other individuals acting on behalf of Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd.

body.text: Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. prohibits all forms of bribery, corruption, kickbacks, facilitation payments, improper gifts, unauthorized donations and any other sensitive transactions intended to influence business decisions or obtain an unfair advantage.
Employees shall not offer, solicit, accept, or provide any gift, payment, hospitality, favor, service, or benefit that could influence, or appear to influence, business decisions.

All procurement, vendor selection, contracting and financial decisions shall be based solely on legitimate business considerations such as quality, cost, capability, compliance and business requirements.
Employees shall immediately disclose any offer, request, or circumstance that may involve:

Gifts or hospitality of inappropriate value.
Personal benefits from suppliers, customers, or business partners.
Conflicts of interest.
Requests for unofficial payments or favors.
Any activity that may compromise ethical business conduct.
The Company shall maintain transparency in business dealings through appropriate documentation, financial controls and management oversight.

blocks.text: The following types of transactions are strictly prohibited at Naxpar Pharma, regardless of value or intent:

Bribes, kickbacks, facilitation payments, or improper commissions.
Cash payments or cash equivalents intended to influence decisions.
Gifts, hospitality, or entertainment that may affect impartial judgment.
Personal benefits received in exchange for business favors.
Undisclosed conflicts of interest.
Unauthorized donations or sponsorships.
Procurement decisions influenced by personal relationships or benefits.
Manipulation of records or transactions to conceal improper activities.
Employees are encouraged to report any suspected violation of this procedure to their Department Head or Management.
All concerns shall be treated confidentially and investigated appropriately. Retaliation against any individual who reports a concern in good faith shall not be tolerated.

Any violation of this procedure may result in disciplinary action, including termination of employment, depending on the nature and severity of the violation. Where applicable, legal action may also be pursued.

responsibilities: Comply with this procedure, avoid prohibited transactions and report any suspected violations.

blocks.text: Management shall review this procedure periodically to ensure its effectiveness and compliance with applicable legal and ethical requirements. sops.title: Anti-Corruption and Information Security Due Diligence Program on Third Parties

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to establish a framework for conducting due diligence on third parties to identify and mitigate risks related to unethical business practices, corruption and information security. This process enables Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. to engage with business partners that operate in accordance with legal requirements, ethical standards and information security expectations.
This procedure applies to suppliers, contractors, service providers, consultants and other third parties engaged or considered for engagement by Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd.

body.text: Prior to engagement, the concerned department shall identify the third party and assess the nature of the proposed business relationship, services to be provided and potential risk exposure.
The third party shall undergo a due diligence review to assess its compliance with ethical business practices and information security requirements. The assessment may include review of:

Business registration and statutory compliance documents.
Previous business performance and reputation.
Compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
Policies and practices related to ethics, anti-corruption and information security.
Ability to protect confidential and business-sensitive information.

As part of the due diligence process, Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. may conduct on-site audits of third-party facilities to verify compliance with ethics and information security requirements.

The audit may include evaluation of:

Ethical business conduct and integrity practices.
Controls to prevent bribery, corruption and conflicts of interest.
Compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Protection and handling of confidential information.
Physical and administrative controls implemented to safeguard information assets.
Relevant records, procedures and management practices.
Audit findings shall be documented and considered during the supplier evaluation and approval process.

The results of the due diligence assessment and on-site audit findings shall be reviewed prior to establishing or continuing the business relationship. Where necessary, corrective actions may be requested before approval is granted.

Naxpar Pharma Pvt. Ltd. shall periodically review third-party performance and compliance through supplier evaluations, business reviews and follow-up audits, where applicable. Any identified concerns relating to ethics, corruption, or information security shall be addressed through appropriate corrective actions.

responsibilities: Conduct due diligence activities and coordinate audits.
Review findings and approve necessary actions.
Cooperate during assessments and provide required information.
